scope: Three already-retained Windows RAM images from the instrumented native Codex app-server cohort
discovery: After both previously frozen methods returned zero candidates on the museum image, a separate complete response.create object was found in its native-process user mappings. Its client_metadata supplied thread_id and turn_id; its input contained one human user.text item for that turn. A task_complete object supplied the response under the same turn_id.
experimental_role: Post-hoc development on museum, then hash-frozen before retrospective checks on lighthouse and observatory. These three images all predate the new method; the later fresh-turn check is reported separately in CLI_REQUEST_CORE_PROSPECTIVE_20261001.json.
selection: Image-derived native codex.exe PID and its resident user-space Volatility memmap; the relay PID was scanned separately in each image
join: One complete response.create object with metadata thread/turn IDs and exactly one input item tagged user.text for that turn; one task_complete with the same turn ID; conflicting bindings or variants are not accepted
field_boundary: The model-input message ID is recovered but was not independently scored. The API user-item ID and a turn-bound assistant-message ID are not recovered by this method.
negative_result_preserved: The museum core-v1 and model-input-v1 frozen scores remain zero. The new request/core join is a different post-hoc grammar and does not retroactively change those scores.
